skills.content:
---
name: Podcast Clipper
description: >-
  When the owner shares a podcast or YouTube episode URL (or a watched channel
  drops a new episode) and wants 8-12 square captioned clips with X post
  versions for each.
---
# Podcast Clipper

Turns one episode into 8-12 square (1080x1080) captioned clips of 20-90s, each with 3-5 X post versions in the owner's voice.

## 0. Setup (once per box)
```bash
pip install --user -U yt-dlp faster-whisper "opencv-python-headless<5" numpy onnxruntime
mkdir -p /workspace/podcast-clips/models && curl -fsSL -o /workspace/podcast-clips/models/yolov8n.onnx https://huggingface.co/Kalray/yolov8/resolve/main/yolov8n.onnx   # person detector for over-shoulder check (optional: without it only the no-face rule applies)
curl -fsSL https://deno.land/install.sh | sh -s -- -y   # yt-dlp needs a JS runtime to pass YouTube's bot check
sudo apt-get install -y ffmpeg fonts-dejavu-core          # ffmpeg must have libass (ass filter)
mkdir -p /workspace/podcast-clips
```
Write the four scripts below into /workspace/podcast-clips/ if missing (`chmod +x fetch_transcribe.sh`).
Notes: faster-whisper 1.2.1 breaks with PyAV 19 when given a file path, so transcribe.py reads the wav with `wave` and passes a numpy array (no PyAV decode). The box is CPU-only; small.en int8 does a ~100 min episode in roughly 20-40 min, so run it in the background. When rendering in a shell loop, pass `</dev/null` to render_clip.py, or ffmpeg will swallow the loop's input.

## 1. Download + transcribe
`/workspace/podcast-clips/fetch_transcribe.sh <url> <slug>` -> `<slug>/video.mp4`, `video.info.json`, `audio.wav` (16k mono), `transcript.txt` (timestamped), `words.json` (word timestamps). Use the info.json chapters to orient.

## 2. Pick moments
Read transcript.txt. Pick 8-12 moments of 20-90s that match the owner's niche/angles (from memory). Prefer a single clear claim, a surprising number, a sharp question and answer, or a quotable line. Each must stand alone without context. Write `picks.txt`, one per line: `NN HH:MM:SS HH:MM:SS`.

## 3. Snap to sentences
`python3 snap.py <slug>/words.json picks.txt` prints exact start/end seconds snapped to segment boundaries plus the text. Adjust picks if a clip starts or ends mid-thought.

## 4. Render
`python3 render_clip.py <slug> NN <start> <end>` for each -> `<slug>/clips/clip-NN.mp4`: face-centred crop per camera shot (Haar cascade), burned-in ASS captions (bold white, black outline, bottom third, ~34 chars/line), H.264 high/yuv420p + AAC, +faststart.

## 5. Verify every clip
```bash
ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=codec_name,width,height -show_entries format=duration -of compact clip-NN.mp4
ffmpeg -v error -i clip-NN.mp4 -f null -   # must print nothing
```
Grab a frame (`ffmpeg -ss 5 -i clip-NN.mp4 -frames:v 1 f.png`) and look at it: face in frame, captions readable, note any on-screen chart or text cut off by the crop.

## 5b. Story QA (required before delivery)
For every clip, print from words.json the sentence before the start, the clip's sentences, and the next two sentences after the end. Fail and re-cut any clip that misses one of these checks:
1. **Clean start**: it opens at the start of a thought, not mid-sentence or partway through someone else's point. Trim the lead-in rather than starting on a fragment.
2. **Complete payoff**: a question includes the full answer, and a setup includes its punchline. Never end on a question unless the answer is in the clip. If the answer is long, trim the question's lead-in instead of the answer. If an answer opens with "Well," or "Only X", include the question it replies to.
3. **Clean end**: it ends on a full sentence that lands. No trailing first words of the next topic (also check the last caption line in the .ass file), and no new question.
4. **Caption-only read**: reading only the captions makes sense to someone who never heard the episode. Pronouns and "that" need a referent inside the clip.
5. **Picture**: extract 4 to 6 frames (`ffmpeg -ss T -i clip.mp4 -frames:v 1 f.png`) and look at them. Faces must be centred and charts or slides not cut off. Shots with no frontal face, and over-the-shoulder shots (a faceless near-full-height person box overlapping the crop), are letterboxed full-frame with captions in the bottom bar (set FIT_NOFACE=0 to turn off the no-face rule). Confirm over-shoulder shots show full-frame. Captions replace 'Grokbot' with 'Grok', a known ASR error; add other fixes to the re.sub line. Re-render if a chart is still cropped.
6. **Overlap**: if two clips cover the same answer, keep the better one and re-cut or drop the other.
Keep the replaced file as clip-NN-old.mp4, update clips.txt, and re-run ffprobe on every changed clip. Note any transcription errors (names, products) in the delivery notes.

## 6. Write posts
For each clip write 3-5 versions (owner's chosen count) following the owner's saved style notes, e.g. story, punchy, reflective, plus optional contrarian or question-led. Rules:
- Hook names who is speaking and why it matters.
- Quote only what the transcript says, and flag that auto-transcripts can mishear names and products, so the owner should listen back before quoting word for word.
- Never invent personal experiences or claims for the owner.
- Source link goes in the first reply, not the post.
- Drafts only. The owner posts.

## 7. Deliver
Send one message per clip: clip number, start-end timestamps, one-line summary/key quote, any crop or transcript caveats, the post versions, and the MP4 attached. Lead with a short note that all clips are done plus the source link.

---
## Scripts

### /workspace/podcast-clips/fetch_transcribe.sh
```bash
#!/bin/bash
export PATH="$HOME/.deno/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
# usage: fetch_transcribe.sh <youtube_url> <slug>
set -e
URL="$1"; SLUG="$2"; D=/workspace/podcast-clips/$SLUG; mkdir -p "$D"; cd "$D"
Y=~/.local/bin/yt-dlp
[ -f video.mp4 ] || $Y -f "bv*[height<=1080][ext=mp4]+ba[ext=m4a]/b[ext=mp4]/b" --merge-output-format mp4 -o "video.%(ext)s" --write-info-json "$URL"
[ -f audio.wav ] || ffmpeg -y -loglevel error -i video.mp4 -vn -ac 1 -ar 16000 audio.wav
python3 /workspace/podcast-clips/transcribe.py "$D"
echo DONE "$D"
```

### /workspace/podcast-clips/transcribe.py
```python
# usage: python3 transcribe.py <dir>   (reads audio.wav 16k mono, writes transcript.txt + words.json)
import sys, json, wave, numpy as np
from faster_whisper import WhisperModel
d=sys.argv[1]
w=wave.open(f"{d}/audio.wav"); a=np.frombuffer(w.readframes(w.getnframes()),np.int16).astype(np.float32)/32768
m=WhisperModel("small.en",device="cpu",compute_type="int8",cpu_threads=8)
segs,_=m.transcribe(a,vad_filter=True,word_timestamps=True)
def ts(s): return f"{int(s//3600):02d}:{int(s%3600//60):02d}:{int(s%60):02d}"
out=[]
with open(f"{d}/transcript.txt","w") as f:
  for s in segs:
    f.write(f"[{ts(s.start)}] {s.text.strip()}\n"); f.flush()
    out.append({"start":s.start,"end":s.end,"text":s.text.strip(),"words":[{"s":x.start,"e":x.end,"w":x.word} for x in (s.words or [])]})
json.dump(out,open(f"{d}/words.json","w"))
```

### /workspace/podcast-clips/snap.py
```python
import json,sys
segs=json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
def p(t):
  h,m,s=[int(x) for x in t.split(":")]; return h*3600+m*60+s
for line in open(sys.argv[2]):
  nn,a,b=line.split()
  a,b=p(a),p(b)
  sa=min(segs,key=lambda s:abs(s["start"]-a)); sb=min(segs,key=lambda s:abs(s["end"]-b))
  txt=" ".join(s["text"] for s in segs if sa["start"]<=s["start"]<=sb["start"])
  S=max(0,sa["words"][0]["s"]-0.25) if sa["words"] else sa["start"]; E=(sb["words"][-1]["e"] if sb["words"] else sb["end"])+0.4
  print(f"{nn} {S:.2f} {E:.2f} {E-S:.0f}s | {txt}\n")
```

### /workspace/podcast-clips/render_clip.py
```python
# usage: python3 render_clip.py <episode_dir> <NN> <start_sec> <end_sec>
# env FIT_RANGES="0-28,60-70" (clip seconds): letterbox whole frame for shots overlapping these ranges (split-screen charts)
# -> <dir>/clips/clip-NN.mp4 : 1080x1080, face-centred crop per shot (or full-frame letterbox for over-shoulder/no-face shots, captions in bottom bar), burned-in captions from words.json
import sys, re, json, subprocess, os, numpy as np, cv2
d, nn, S, E = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], float(sys.argv[3]), float(sys.argv[4])
os.makedirs(f"{d}/clips", exist_ok=True); tmp=f"{d}/clips/.tmp-{nn}.mp4"; ass=f"{d}/clips/clip-{nn}.ass"; out=f"{d}/clips/clip-{nn}.mp4"
subprocess.run(["ffmpeg","-y","-loglevel","error","-ss",str(S),"-i",f"{d}/video.mp4","-t",str(E-S),"-c:v","libx264","-preset","ultrafast","-crf","16","-c:a","aac","-b:a","192k",tmp],check=True)
import onnxruntime as ort
MODEL=os.environ.get("YOLO_ONNX",os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)),"models","yolov8n.onnx"))
yolo=ort.InferenceSession(MODEL,providers=["CPUExecutionProvider"]) if os.path.exists(MODEL) else None
def persons(f):
  if yolo is None: return []
  h0,w0=f.shape[:2]; r=640/max(w0,h0); im=cv2.resize(f,(int(w0*r),int(h0*r))); pad=np.full((640,640,3),114,np.uint8); pad[:im.shape[0],:im.shape[1]]=im
  p=yolo.run(None,{yolo.get_inputs()[0].name:pad[:,:,::-1].transpose(2,0,1)[None].astype(np.float32)/255})[0][0]
  k=p[4]>0.4; b=p[:4,k].T/r; sc=p[4,k]
  if not len(b): return []
  bx=[[float(x-w/2),float(y-h/2),float(w),float(h)] for x,y,w,h in b]
  return [(bx[i][0],bx[i][1],bx[i][0]+bx[i][2],bx[i][1]+bx[i][3]) for i in np.array(cv2.dnn.NMSBoxes(bx,sc.tolist(),0.4,0.5)).flatten()]
cap=cv2.VideoCapture(tmp); fps=cap.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FPS); W=int(cap.get(3)); H=int(cap.get(4)); side=min(W,H)
fc=cv2.CascadeClassifier(cv2.data.haarcascades+"haarcascade_frontalface_default.xml")
hists=[]; grays=[]; samp={}
i=0
while True:
  ok,f=cap.read()
  if not ok: break
  small=cv2.resize(f,(320,180)); h=cv2.calcHist([cv2.cvtColor(small,cv2.COLOR_BGR2HSV)],[0,1],None,[16,16],[0,180,0,256]); cv2.normalize(h,h)
  hists.append(h); grays.append(cv2.cvtColor(cv2.resize(small,(64,36)),cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY).astype(np.int16))
  if i%int(fps/3 or 1)==0:
    g=cv2.cvtColor(cv2.resize(f,(960,540)),cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    fs=[(x*W/960,y*H/540,w*W/960,h_*H/540) for x,y,w,h_ in fc.detectMultiScale(g,1.1,6,minSize=(50,50))]
    if fs:
      x,y,w,h_=max(fs,key=lambda r:r[2]*r[3]); c=min(max(x+w/2,side/2),W-side/2); x0,x1=c-side/2,c+side/2; back=False
      for a in persons(f):
        if any(a[0]<=fx+fw/2<=a[2] and a[1]<=fy+fh/2<=a[3] for fx,fy,fw,fh in fs): continue
        if a[3]-a[1]>0.6*H and min(a[2],x1)-max(a[0],x0)>0.03*side: back=True; break
      samp[i]=(x+w/2,back)
    else: samp[i]=(None,False)
  i+=1
n=i
cuts=[0]+[k for k in range(1,n) if cv2.compareHist(hists[k-1],hists[k],cv2.HISTCMP_CORREL)<0.6 or np.abs(grays[k]-grays[k-1]).mean()>28]+[n]
cx=np.zeros(n); fit=np.zeros(n,bool); fitshots=[]
ranges=[r for r in os.environ.get("FIT_RANGES","").split(",") if r]
for a,b in zip(cuts[:-1],cuts[1:]):
  ss=[samp[k] for k in samp if a<=k<b]; v=[c for c,bk in ss if c is not None]
  c=np.median(v) if v else W/2; cx[a:b]=min(max(c,side/2),W-side/2)
  noface=len(v)<0.5*max(len(ss),1); back=sum(bk for _,bk in ss)>=0.4*max(len(ss),1)
  forced=any(float(r.split("-")[0])*fps<b and a<float(r.split("-")[1])*fps for r in ranges)
  fit[a:b]=(noface and os.environ.get("FIT_NOFACE","1")=="1") or back or forced
  if fit[a]: fitshots.append(f"{a/fps:.1f}-{b/fps:.1f}s({'chart' if forced else 'back' if back else 'noface'})")
words=[w for s in json.load(open(f"{d}/words.json")) for w in s["words"] if w["e"]>S and w["s"]<E]
def t(x): x=max(0,x-S); return f"{int(x//3600)}:{int(x%3600//60):02d}:{x%60:05.2f}"
chunks=[];cur=[]
for w in words:
  if cur and (len(" ".join(c["w"].strip() for c in cur+[w]))>34 or w["s"]-cur[-1]["e"]>0.7): chunks.append(cur);cur=[]
  cur.append(w)
  if w["w"].strip()[-1:] in ".?!": chunks.append(cur);cur=[]
if cur: chunks.append(cur)
with open(ass,"w") as f:
  f.write("[Script Info]\nScriptType: v4.00+\nPlayResX: 1080\nPlayResY: 1080\nWrapStyle: 0\n\n[V4+ Styles]\nFormat: Name, Fontname, Fontsize, PrimaryColour, SecondaryColour, OutlineColour, BackColour, Bold, Italic, Underline, StrikeOut, ScaleX, ScaleY, Spacing, Angle, BorderStyle, Outline, Shadow, Alignment, MarginL, MarginR, MarginV, Encoding\n")
  f.write("Style: Cap,DejaVu Sans,66,&H00FFFFFF,&H00FFFFFF,&H00000000,&H80000000,-1,0,0,0,100,100,0,0,1,6,2,2,70,70,170,1\n")
  f.write("Style: Bar,DejaVu Sans,54,&H00FFFFFF,&H00FFFFFF,&H00000000,&H80000000,-1,0,0,0,100,100,0,0,1,4,1,2,50,50,40,1\n\n[Events]\nFormat: Layer, Start, End, Style, Name, MarginL, MarginR, MarginV, Effect, Text\n")
  for k,c in enumerate(chunks):
    end=c[-1]["e"]
    if k+1<len(chunks): end=min(max(end,c[-1]["e"]+0.3),chunks[k+1][0]["s"])
    txt=re.sub(r"(?i)\bgrok ?bot\b","Grok"," ".join(x['w'].strip() for x in c))
    a0=c[0]['s']; fr=lambda x:min(n-1,max(0,int((x-S)*fps)))
    sw=[S+k/fps for k in range(fr(a0)+1,fr(end)+1) if fit[k]!=fit[k-1]]
    for p0,p1 in zip([a0]+sw,sw+[end]):
      f.write(f"Dialogue: 0,{t(p0)},{t(p1)},{'Bar' if fit[fr(p0+0.01)] else 'Cap'},,0,0,0,,{txt}\n")
p=subprocess.Popen(["ffmpeg","-y","-loglevel","error","-f","rawvideo","-pix_fmt","bgr24","-s",f"{side}x{side}","-r",str(fps),"-i","-","-i",tmp,"-map","0:v","-map","1:a","-vf",f"scale=1080:1080,ass={ass}","-c:v","libx264","-preset","medium","-crf","20","-pix_fmt","yuv420p","-profile:v","high","-c:a","aac","-b:a","128k","-ar","44100","-movflags","+faststart","-shortest",out],stdin=subprocess.PIPE)
cap=cv2.VideoCapture(tmp); k=0
while True:
  ok,f=cap.read()
  if not ok: break
  kk=min(k,n-1)
  if fit[kk]:
    hh=int(H*side/W); fr=np.zeros((side,side,3),np.uint8); y0=(side-hh)//2; fr[y0:y0+hh]=cv2.resize(f,(side,hh)); p.stdin.write(fr.tobytes())
  else:
    x0=int(cx[kk]-side/2); p.stdin.write(np.ascontiguousarray(f[(H-side)//2:(H-side)//2+side,x0:x0+side]).tobytes())
  k+=1
p.stdin.close(); p.wait(); os.remove(tmp); print(out, "shots:",len(cuts)-1, "full-frame:", ", ".join(fitshots) or "none")
```

skills.name: Podcast Clipper Getting Started
skills.description: First conversation with a new owner of the Podcast Clipper bot, or when the owner asks to set up or change which podcasts, niche, voice or clip settings it uses.
skills.content:
---
name: Podcast Clipper Getting Started
description: >-
  First conversation with a new owner of the Podcast Clipper bot, or when the
  owner asks to set up or change which podcasts, niche, voice or clip settings
  it uses.
---
# Getting started

Open with one line: "I turn podcast episodes into 8-12 square, captioned clips, each with ready-to-post X drafts in your voice."

Then ask ONE question at a time, waiting for each answer:
1. Which podcasts or YouTube channels should I watch? (names or URLs)
2. What's your niche, and which angles do you want clips to hit? (e.g. AI chips, investing, founders)
3. What's your X handle? Paste or link 3-5 of your own posts you like so I can learn your voice.
4. How many post versions per clip, 3, 4 or 5?
5. Want me to watch those channels and clip new episodes automatically when they drop?

After the answers:
- Save memories: watched sources (with channel URLs), niche/angles, X handle, versions per clip, auto-watch yes/no.
- Read the posts they gave (fetch them if linked) and save style notes as a memory: length, tone, hook style, emoji use, punctuation habits, words they avoid. Never invent personal facts about the owner.
- If auto-watch is yes: create a routine (e.g. hourly, or every 15 min on known release days) that checks each source for an episode newer than the last one recorded in memory; when one appears, tell the owner it dropped, run the Podcast Clipper skill on it, and record it as processed so it's never clipped twice.
- Confirm the setup back in 2-3 lines and offer to clip a recent episode now as a test.
